project.prefix_rationale: The Authority Gate builds its work-package pattern from this value instead of hard-coding it (SECB-WP-FWK-036, NFR-15). A project instantiated from this framework edits this string; before it existed, a new project's gate rejected every pull request until someone found the regex inside scripts/check_work_package_ref.py. Uppercase alphanumerics and hyphens only -- the gate refuses anything else rather than compiling a pattern that might match everything, which would fail open.

authority_source: Operator (vily), Genesis Ratification by merge of SECB-WP-FWK-012 (issue #20)

signature.reason: Cryptographic envelope signing requires a trust anchor outside this repository (see docs/14-plans/GOVERNANCE_DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES.md). Until then the envelope's integrity rests on git history and the human merge that ratified it, and the classifier treats an unsigned envelope as valid ONLY for tiers at or below the ratified tier.

A1.authority: Low-risk (G0) auto-merge inside the envelope scope
advance_conditions: 30 consecutive auto-merged PRs with zero rollback
no CONSTITUTIONAL_REQUIRED verdict misclassified as lower

A3.authority: Governance implementation (G1) without fresh human approval
advance_conditions: 60 days of shadow-mode evidence comparing base and head gate decisions

A4.authority: Scope and ceiling adjustment inside the L0 absolute maxima (G2)
advance_conditions: full ballot quorum with no veto
rollback verified by execution, not by description

ballot_layer.reason: Five independent agents with separately enforced service identities do not exist in this deployment. One session emitting five role-labelled ballots is self-approval in five hats; role banners are self-asserted text and must never gate a decision. Quorum is therefore not enforced anywhere in code, and every verdict that would depend on it escalates instead.
ballot_layer.quorum_when_active: 4 of 5, with governance and security holding veto; 5 of 5 for G2-G3

gate_activation.note: A change to a gate script merges INACTIVE and takes effect in the next governance epoch, so no PR is judged by the gate it introduces. Enforced today by the dual-policy rule (base and head logic must agree); full epoch machinery is deferred.
